actions: Inspect the identified source skill, required test-result field, and affected references/resources; retain its established model, runtime, output contract, and authorization.

Edit the source instructions so release-note prose is Japanese while the existing required test-result field and semantics remain intact. Apply skill-creator if the change actually revises skill structure, and relevant prompt-design guidance for the instruction change.

Review representative release-note cases with supplied and missing test evidence: confirm Japanese output, retention of the required field, and no invented test outcomes. Preserve the existing contract for missing information.
Run the identified repository check on the final source state. Reuse its package and skill validation rather than duplicating those validators.
Read back the final instructions and report changed source files and checks. Retain the existing direct-source link; no installation or link deactivation is required.
completion: The source skill specifies Japanese release notes and preserves the required test-result contract.
Affected instruction review and the repository package/skill check pass on the final source.
Report simulated cases as simulations; this source change can finish without installation or a newly created task.
limitations: The fixture omits actual skill text and repository command names, so exact edits and the existing check command must be selected from the identified source during real execution.
An existing task may retain earlier instructions. A direct source link does not establish plugin installation or cache freshness.

actions: Read the native manifest, MCP configuration, skill, hook, and relevant documentation without changing files or client state.
Verify current portable specification mappings and any official client documentation relevant to the hook. Do not install merely to fill a findings-only review.
Report that the contained skill is a portable candidate after validation and that supported .mcp.json content requires semantic conversion to root mcp.json rather than only renaming.
Explain the future root plugin.json mapping and eventual removal of .codex-plugin/plugin.json from a portable source; perform neither during this review.

Flag the required hook as an unresolved compatibility boundary because no documented extension has been found. Describe a separate derived Codex-native distribution as a preservation option; do not invent an extension namespace or silently omit the hook.
Return findings and evidence limits only.
completion: Findings account for all supplied native components and explain the portable mapping and required-hook limitation.
The review distinguishes source feasibility from verified client behavior and describes an actionable migration option without implementing it.
limitations: The absence of a documented hook extension in the case is not proof that all current or future clients reject it.
Equivalent hook behavior and runtime operation remain unverified. A materially different distribution arrangement can be resolved when actual migration is requested.

actions: Use the exact identified source and team-dev Marketplace. Inspect the existing repository manager and CLI help; prefer the repository command when available.
Confirm the named Marketplace root and current snapshot using sufficiently current evidence or read-only commands: codex plugin marketplace list --json and codex plugin list --available --json.
Select --keep-version directly from the user's instruction to preserve the release version. Do not ask for another version-policy choice or scaffold a policy.

Invoke the existing repository install command with --keep-version and its established Marketplace binding. If no repository manager exists, use: node <skill-root>/scripts/manage-local-agent-plugin.mjs install <source-root> --marketplace-root <team-dev-root> --keep-version.

Let install perform its included validation/checks before mutation, without manually duplicating checks already established for the same state. Register the matching Marketplace only if necessary; do not uninstall first.

Verify installed identity, team-dev membership, source path when reported, snapshot, manifest version 2.3.0, and enabled state. Exercise discovery on an already authorized new-task surface when available; otherwise report that check as outstanding without creating a task.
completion: The intended plugin is installed and enabled locally from team-dev, with snapshot and manifest matching source identity and version 2.3.0.
The source version is unchanged, and installation evidence is reported separately from any untested new-task discovery or behavior.
limitations: Actual plugin name, paths, and repository entrypoint are not supplied in the fixture.
The manager does not verify enabled state or execution; matching name/version does not establish byte-for-byte resource equality.
Creating an additional Codex task requires explicit authorization and is not supplied here.

actions: Recover the retained operation/session result if available. Determine whether the original manager or Codex child is running and use the runtime's supported wait/result mechanism before any conflicting reinstall, version edit, or restoration.

After the operation finishes or is reconciled, inspect source plugin.json, any retained install result, Marketplace registration, and current snapshot. Read-only examples: codex plugin marketplace list --json and codex plugin list --available --json.
Keep the intended candidate version 2.3.0+agent.20260906070000000 if the source still matches the validated candidate. Do not infer failure or rollback from the lost response.
If the intended version is already installed, perform only missing snapshot, enabled-state, freshness, and authorized new-task discovery checks.

If installation is incomplete and the candidate is unchanged, resume under existing authority and repository policy with --keep-version. Use the established repository manager, or node <skill-root>/scripts/manage-local-agent-plugin.mjs install <source-root> --marketplace-root <expected-marketplace-root> --keep-version when that is the established path and contract permits it.
Report the source-version effect, registration, installation result, and remaining verification separately. Do not perform speculative restoration or a second bump.
completion: No conflicting installation operation remains in flight.
The intended candidate is installed under the expected identity and Marketplace, with snapshot and enabled state verified.
Retry has not introduced another version bump, and any remaining discovery limitation is explicit.
limitations: Operation handle, final result, and present snapshot are absent; the next mutation depends on reconciliation.
The manager is not transactional and has no cross-process lock. Version and registration may remain even after an installation failure.
A changed candidate or stricter repository contract found during inspection must be reconciled before using the keep-version retry.

actions: Read the generated catalog to obtain the actual Marketplace name and confirm atlas resolves to its generated package at version 1.2.0.
Inspect current CLI help, registration, snapshot, and only relevant same-named direct links. Isolate or deactivate conflicting atlas links within the authorized installation scope if needed.
Register the assembled root only when necessary: codex plugin marketplace add <assembled-marketplace-root>.
Install through the consumer CLI: codex plugin add 'atlas@<catalog-marketplace-name>'. Do not use the developer manager on a generated package.
Verify installed atlas identity, Marketplace, reported source root, snapshot, version 1.2.0, and enabled state. Use an already authorized new-task surface for discovery or report that limit.
Keep source tests and version policy upstream. Do not require unavailable original repositories or invoke source synchronization, assembly, or source-drift checks as a consumer prerequisite.
completion: Atlas 1.2.0 is installed and enabled from the intended assembled Marketplace, with identity and snapshot verified.
Any unperformed discovery or behavior check is reported.
limitations: This consumer can inspect generated content and install it but cannot certify upstream source-to-distribution drift or repository tests.
The Marketplace name must come from the catalog rather than being invented.
No additional Codex task may be created without explicit authorization.

actions: Inspect the existing orchestrator's scoped-sync interface and atlas contributor binding. Preserve its private configuration, source-free reference, ownership scope, and version relationship.
Reuse passing atlas source checks for the same candidate; no catalog membership change is required.
Invoke the orchestrator's supported scoped sync for atlas, keeping its Marketplace-wide writer lock across reference reading, underlying assembly, and reference update.

Let the orchestrator supply its private effective definition with unrelated generated copies as catalog context. Its underlying operation may use sync <marketplace-root> --config <orchestrator-effective-config> --plugin atlas --merge; do not improvise this configuration or invoke manual merge outside its ownership.
Run the corresponding orchestrator scoped check for atlas and inspect selected copy, catalog entry, digest/state, and reference results. Preserve unrelated entries and content.
If sync fails or its response is lost, reconcile reference, catalogs, digests, selected source, and active writer under the same ownership before retrying.
completion: The shared atlas copy matches the validated source and its scoped check passes.
Unrelated packages and membership are preserved, and the report certifies atlas only.
limitations: The fixture supplies orchestrator capabilities but no command spelling; select its concrete entrypoint from existing help.
This scoped handoff does not require a full Marketplace check or unrelated source repositories.
The direct assembler has no writer lock, and sync is not transactional across all outputs.

actions: Inspect applicable repository instructions and select the smallest suitable plugin root. The request and repository resolve the format to portable Agent Plugins v1.

Use skill-creator for the contained checklist skill, preserving supplied content and adding a focused capability-and-trigger description. Apply relevant prompt-design guidance using GPT-6 Astra as the authoring design target because the intended runtime is Codex and no model is established; do not add this target to portable metadata or alter client settings.
Verify current version-sensitive package and skill fields against the Agent Plugins and Agent Skills specifications before finalizing.

Create <plugin-root>/plugin.json with {"$schema":"https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json","name":"change-checklist"} and <plugin-root>/skills/change-checklist/SKILL.md with matching skill name, trigger description, and supplied checklist instructions.
Omit unsupported optional metadata and unnecessary scaffolding: no invented release version, repository manager/configuration, Marketplace, MCP configuration, native manifest, or client extension.

Run applicable repository checks, portable validation such as node <skill-root>/scripts/validate-agent-plugin.mjs <plugin-root>, and an available skill validator after checking its coverage. Reuse validation already covered by a repository command.
Review a representative activation/task case, read back the final files, and report the source and verification limits.
completion: A minimal portable source named change-checklist contains the requested immediate-child checklist skill and preserves the supplied content.
Manifest and skill validation pass, with representative instruction review supporting its intended use.
Source delivery completes the request without registration, installation, release policy, or an additional task.
limitations: Actual checklist content and repository layout are fixture inputs but are not included in the test description; actual files must follow those inputs.
Structural validation does not establish runtime behavior. GPT-6 Astra is an authoring design target, not a runtime requirement.
If normative lookup fails, identify the retrieval failure and last-known guidance, continue independent work, and defer only version-sensitive decisions requiring unavailable evidence.
